# Consular Services The consular desk serves American citizens living, working or stranded on this colony. Bring your identity card. A contract is not a passport.
## For Citizens - [bold]Registration[/bold]: tell the mission you are here. In an evacuation, the mission can only account for the names on its list. - [bold]Travel documents[/bold]: replacement of lost, stolen or confiscated passports. Emergency travel papers are issued the same shift where the need is real. - [bold]Births, marriages and deaths[/bold]: recorded and certified so they stand on Earth and on every UA world. - [bold]Notarial services[/bold]: witnessing of signatures, wills and powers of attorney. - [bold]Absentee ballots[/bold]: collected and sent home with the diplomatic pouch.
## In an Emergency - [bold]Arrest or detention[/bold]: you have the right to ask that the mission be told. A consular officer will visit, see that you are fed and treated fairly, and find you counsel. The mission cannot overturn a lawful arrest. - [bold]Injury or illness[/bold]: the mission will contact your family and help arrange treatment or medical evacuation. - [bold]Repatriation[/bold]: citizens left destitute by a failed contract or a closed site may apply for passage home, repaid by loan.
## What We Cannot Do - Settle wage or contract disputes with your employer. Take these to [netlink="Colonial Administration" link="admin.colony.gov"] or to the Colonial Marshals. - Pay fines, bail or debts on your behalf. - Help anyone who has given money, shelter or arms to the [bold]Colonial Liberation Front[/bold]. Material support for a designated terrorist group is a federal crime, wherever it is committed.
## Hours The desk keeps colony shift hours. Out of hours, reply to any communique and mark it [bold]URGENT[/bold].
